title: Caffeine-Timing vs Sleep-Quality Correlation
dataSources: HRV (`hrv:reading`), blood oxygen (`spo2:reading`), lab panels (`bloodpanel:result`), supplements (`supplement:intake`), continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), sleep-apnea events (`apnea:event`), body composition (`bodycomp:measure`).
app: Biohacking and advanced-health data — HRV chest straps, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure cuffs, continuous glucose monitors, body-composition scales, lab-result exports, and supplement logs — ingested to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=espresso:shot OR sourcetype=oura:daily)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(strftime(_time,"%H")>=14,caffeine_mg,0))) as late_caffeine, avg(sleep_score) as sleep by _time
| eval high_late=if(late_caffeine>100,1,0)
| stats avg(sleep) as avg_sleep by high_late
description: Compares your sleep quality on days with and without late-afternoon caffeine, testing the advice on your own body.
value: Generic caffeine advice may not fit you; comparing your own late-caffeine days to the rest gives a personal, convincing answer.
implementation: Ingest caffeine timing and sleep scores into `index=personal`; compare average sleep by whether you had late caffeine.
visualization: Bar chart of average sleep score with versus without late caffeine.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Oura Ring — Oura Cloud API v2 → HEC scripted input.
• **Subcategory context**: Advanced Health & Biohacking — typical feeds: HRV (`hrv:reading`), blood oxygen (`spo2:reading`), lab panels (`bloodpanel:result`), supplements (`supplement:intake`), continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), sleep-apnea events (`apnea:event`), body co.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `espresso:shot`, `oura:daily`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Oura Ring** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=espresso:shot`.

**Collection method:** Oura Cloud API v2 → HEC scripted input.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `GET /v2/usercollection/daily_sleep`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 86400s (daily sync).

**Key fields to extract:** `score, contributors, heart_rate, hrv`.

**Typical connector stack:** Biohacking data — HRV straps, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure cuffs, continuous glucose monitors, body-composition scales, lab-result exports, and supplement logs — ingested to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Ingest caffeine timing and sleep scores into `index=personal`; compare average sleep by whether you had late caffeine.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "espresso:shot", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Caffeine-Timing vs Sleep-Quality Correlation** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=espresso:shot`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `late_caffeine` (> 100) after sum, avg — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `high_late`, `late_caffeine`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal (sourcetype=espresso:shot OR sourcetype=oura:daily)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(strftime(_time,"%H")>=14,caffeine_mg,0))) as late_caffeine, avg(sleep_score) as sleep by _time
| eval high_late=if(late_caffeine>100,1,0)
| stats avg(sleep) as avg_sleep by high_late
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Oura app → Readiness / Sleep tabs. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, high_late, late_caffeine
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `late_caffeine` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(late_caffeine) AS p50 perc90(late_caffeine) AS p90 perc99(late_caffeine) AS p99 max(late_caffeine) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.25.10: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Bar Chart Of Average Sleep Score With Versus Without Late Caffeine (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Oura Ring — no Oura Ring events / missing fields:** If `espresso:shot` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Oura Ring connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Oura Ring — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Oura Ring JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Oura Ring — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Oura Ring — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Oura Ring APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how well you sleep on days you had afternoon coffee versus days you did not, testing the advice on you.
